ds: Inherent-risk factors relating to the products and services offered. Covers private banking, correspondent relationships, trade finance, prepaid instruments, virtual assets, safe deposit boxes and cash services.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Generic product risk factors.

rat: Generic product-risk list: private banking, correspondent, trade, prepaid, virtual assets, safe deposit.

ind.cx: High-net-worth relationships with bespoke structures, discretion expectations and large flows.
ind.fp: Most wealth clients are wholly legitimate.
ind.ds: High-net-worth relationships with bespoke structures, discretion expectations and large flows.

ind.cx: Provision of accounts or payment services to other financial institutions that process on behalf of unknown customers.
ind.ds: Provision of accounts or payment services to other financial institutions that process on behalf of unknown customers.

ind.cx: Products reliant on documentation that can be manipulated, with pricing and goods difficult to verify.
ind.ds: Products reliant on documentation that can be manipulated, with pricing and goods difficult to verify.

ind.cx: Anonymous or lightly verified instruments with high load limits or cross-border use.
ind.ds: Prepaid cards or stored-value products without full ID, with high load limits, cross-border use or turnover inconsistent with design.
ind.cn: Anonymous or lightly verified prepaid or stored-value instruments

ind.cx: Provision of services enabling conversion, custody or transfer of virtual assets.
ind.fp: Adoption of virtual assets for legitimate investment is widespread.
ind.ds: Provision of services enabling conversion, custody or transfer of virtual assets.

ind.cx: Physical storage of unknown assets with limited visibility.
ind.ds: Physical storage of unknown assets with limited visibility.

ind.n: Cash services and high-limit cash handling
ind.cx: Services involving large cash deposits, withdrawals, currency exchange or cash-in-transit.
ind.ds: Services involving large cash deposits, withdrawals, currency exchange or cash-in-transit.

ind.cx: Services such as payable-through accounts, pooled accounts or payment agent facilities.
ind.fp: Pooled accounts are standard for professionals.
ind.ds: Underlying customers of another party transact directly through payable-through, pooled or payment-agent facilities.
ind.cn: Payable-through or pooled access enabling third-party payments

ind.n: New or innovative product without risk assessment
ind.cx: Product launched without documented ML/TF risk assessment or controls.
ind.fp: Minor variants may be assessed under existing products.
ind.ds: Product launched without documented ML/TF risk assessment or controls.

ind.cx: Services moving value across borders quickly through multiple intermediaries.
ind.ds: Services moving value across borders quickly through multiple intermediaries.

ind.cx: Products permitting use without full identification, such as mixers, bearer-like instruments or unverified top-ups.
ind.fp: Privacy features can be sought for lawful reasons.
ind.ds: Products permitting use without full identification, such as mixers, bearer-like instruments or unverified top-ups.

ctl.ds: Requires declarations of conflicts from staff and third parties with annual refresh, rotation of relationship managers and challenge of exceptions. It reduces the chance that decisions are shaped by personal interest.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.
Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

Collects, validates and transmits required originator and beneficiary information with virtual asset transfers and holds or blocks transfers where counterparty data is missing or unreliable. It brings wire-like transparency to virtual asset payments.

Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

Secures contractual rights to underlying client information for intermediated or pooled accounts, requires look-through on request and monitors pooled flows against expected activity. It gives visibility of who is really transacting behind an aggregate account.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

Requires financial crime risk assessment and compliance approval before launching or materially changing products and features, with a post-launch review after a set period. It builds controls in before exposure arises.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.
